policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'for they said' renders the causal γάρ; δέ would give a connective 'but/and', not 'for'.
Pure Greek word order (ἔσται θόρυβος / θόρυβος ἔσται); English 'there shall be a tumult' is identical either way.
ASV's 'and she brake the cruse' needs a coordinating 'and' to join the finite clauses whether or not καί stands in the Greek, so the English does not distinguish.
Gender of the article with ἀλάβαστρον only; 'the cruse' is unaffected.
With or without κατά, 'poured it over his head' renders the genitive τῆς κεφαλῆς identically.
English requires a verb of speaking before the direct discourse, so 'saying' may render καὶ λέγοντες or supply what the participle-less base leaves implicit.
ASV 'this ointment' renders τοῦτο τὸ μύρον; the omission would leave only 'this'.
Word order only; 'three hundred shillings' is the same either way.
ASV 'ye can do them good' has no second 'always', so πάντοτε (r01) is excluded; αὐτοῖς and αὐτοὺς both give 'them'.
αὕτη is redundant with the verb's subject; ASV 'She hath done' supplies the pronoun either way.
Position of μου only; 'my body' is identical.
ASV 'And verily I say unto you' renders the connective δέ; the omission leaves asyndeton, which ASV renders without 'And'.
ἐάν and ἄν are orthographic variants of the same generalizing particle in ὅπου ἐάν; 'wheresoever' is unaffected.
ASV reads 'the gospel', not 'this gospel', so τοῦτο is not in the text rendered.
Article with the proper name only; English 'Judas' takes no article.
The ASV note 'Greek the one of the twelve' shows the article standing before εἷς, which the RP order (ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης, εἷς) does not have; Ἰσκαριώθ and Ἰσκαριώτης both give 'Iscariot'.
ASV 'deliver him unto them' renders the dative αὐτοῖς; the RP reading has only αὐτόν and no 'unto them'.
Word order and the παραδοῖ/παραδῷ spelling only; 'how he might conveniently deliver him' is unchanged.
ἐάν and ἄν are variants of the same particle after ὅπου; 'wheresoever' is unaffected.
ASV 'my guest-chamber' renders μου; the omission gives simply 'the guest-chamber'.
ASV opens 'And he will himself show you', rendering the connective καί that the RP reading omits.
ASV reads 'the disciples', not 'his disciples', so αὐτοῦ is absent.
Order of ὁ Ἰησοῦς and εἶπεν only; 'Jesus said' is the English either way.
English supplies the subject pronoun 'They' in both readings, and the ASV's sentence break leaves οἱ δέ undecidable.
ASV ends the verse at 'Is it I?' with no second 'And another said, Is it I?', excluding the RP addition.
ASV 'And he said unto them' has no 'answered', so ἀποκριθείς is not rendered.
εἷς τῶν δώδεκα and εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα both give 'one of the twelve'.
ASV 'in the dish' lacks 'the one dish', so ἕν is not in the text rendered.
ASV 'For the Son of man goeth' renders ὅτι; the omission leaves the clause without 'For'.
English counterfactual 'good were it for that man' uses the past subjunctive whether or not ἦν stands in the Greek.
ASV 'he took bread' keeps the pronoun subject; the addition would give 'Jesus took'.
ASV 'Take ye: this is my body' has no 'eat', excluding φάγετε.
ASV 'a cup' renders the anarthrous ποτήριον; τό would give 'the cup'.
The mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities insert new' places καινῆς outside the ASV text, excluding r02; the bare article τό leaves no English trace.
Word order and ὑπέρ/περί only; 'poured out for many' renders either.
ASV 'All ye shall be offended' has no 'because of me this night', excluding the RP expansion.
Word order and verb number only; 'the sheep shall be scattered abroad' is unchanged.
Εἰ καί and Καὶ εἰ are both concessive here and both are rendered 'Although'.
Word order and the presence of ἐν only; 'this night' renders either.
Greek order of με and the verb; English puts the object after 'deny' regardless.
ASV 'he spake exceeding vehemently' renders ἐλάλει and has no 'the more' for μᾶλλον.
Order of δέῃ and με only; 'If I must die' is unchanged.
Future indicative and aorist subjunctive both yield 'I will not deny thee' after οὐ μή.
Articles with the proper names only; 'James and John' is unaffected.
αὐτοῦ and ἑαυτοῦ both give 'with him'.
ASV 'he went forward a little' renders προελθών (advance), not προσελθών (approach).
Word order only; 'remove this cup from me' renders either.
ἔλθητε and εἰσέλθητε with εἰς πειρασμόν are both rendered 'enter not into temptation'.
ASV 'And again he came' has πάλιν with a verb of coming: r01 lacks πάλιν and r02 reads ὑποστρέψας, 'returned'.
Position of αὐτῶν only; 'their eyes' is unchanged.
καταβαρυνόμενοι and βεβαρημένοι are both rendered 'very heavy'.
Word order only; 'what to answer him' renders either.
Article with λοιπόν only; the adverbial phrase is rendered the same.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same adverb, both 'straightway'.
ASV reads only 'Judas' here, with no 'Iscariot', excluding r02; the article leaves no English trace.
The added participle ὤν is not separately rendered in 'one of the twelve'.
ASV 'a multitude', not 'a great multitude', excludes πολύς.
ἀπάγετε and ἀπαγάγετε both give 'lead him away'.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same adverb, both 'straightway'.
ASV 'saith, Rabbi' has the address once and without a dative 'to him', excluding the doubled RP reading.
ASV 'they laid hands on him' has no possessive 'their hands' for αὐτῶν.
ASV 'a certain one of them that stood by' renders τις, which Treg omits.
ὠτάριον and ὠτίον are both rendered 'ear'.
Word order only; 'they all left him, and fled' renders either.
'a certain young man' renders νεανίσκος τις and εἷς τις νεανίσκος alike; the indefinite εἷς τις is not separately expressed in English.
ASV 'followed with him' renders the συν- compound συνηκολούθει; ἠκολούθησεν would give simply 'followed him'.
ASV 'they lay hold on him' has no expressed subject 'the young men' for οἱ νεανίσκοι.
ASV 'fled naked' has no 'from them' for ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν.
ASV 'there come together with him all the chief priests' renders the dative αὐτῷ, which the base lacks.
Greek negation pattern and order only; 'answered nothing' renders either.
Word order only; 'to be worthy of death' renders either.
Position of αὐτοῦ only; 'his face' is unchanged.
ASV 'the officers received him with blows' renders ἔλαβον; ἔβαλλον would be 'struck/cast', not 'received'.
Word order only; 'beneath in the court' renders either.
ASV 'with the Nazarene, even Jesus' renders the appositional τοῦ Ἰησοῦ after the verb; RP's attributive Ναζαρηνοῦ Ἰησοῦ would give 'with Jesus of Nazareth'.
ASV 'I neither know, nor understand' renders the correlative οὔτε ... οὔτε; οὐκ ... οὐδέ would give 'I know not, neither understand I'.
The mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities omit and the cock crew' places the clause in the ASV text and the omission in the margin.
Order of ἤρξατο and πάλιν only; 'began again to say' renders either.
παρεστῶσιν and παρεστηκόσιν are the same participle, both 'them that stood by'.
ASV ends at 'for thou art a Galilaean' with nothing for 'and thy speech agreeth thereto', so the clause is absent from the text rendered.
ASV 'And straightway the second time the cock crew' renders εὐθύς, which RP omits.
ASV 'the word, how that Jesus said unto him' renders ὡς; the relative ὅ would give 'the word which Jesus said'.
All three differ only in Greek word order; English fixes 'the cock crow twice' and 'deny me thrice' regardless.
